intent: Stop boot-repair from deleting the only kernel on a BIOS/GRUB system that has no EFI System Partition, without changing its behaviour on kuhy's UEFI machine.
scope: linux_configuration/scripts/boot_recovery/boot-repair (clean_shadow_files, new system_is_uefi helper, header invariants, --esp help text)
Non-goal: fixing the other BIOS-unsafe-but-non-destructive paths (mount_esp, check_fstab_options, run_preflight) -- audited and left alone deliberately
changes: Added GUARD 3 to clean_shadow_files(): when rpath(/sys/firmware/efi) is absent the system booted via BIOS, has no ESP, and /boot holds the real kernel -- warn and return 1 instead of deleting.
Added system_is_uefi(), expressed through rpath() so --root fixtures declare their own firmware type and the guard is testable without a VM; on ROOT=/ it resolves to the real /sys path.
Made the guard overridable via the existing --esp DEVICE rather than adding a new flag: naming the ESP by hand asserts the firmware assumption the guard checks.
Gave make_root() a third 'firmware' parameter defaulting to uefi (creates sys/firmware/efi), so the pre-existing UEFI-shaped fixtures keep their meaning.
Added three cases: BIOS guard refuses and explains, --esp overrides it, and a UEFI fixture still cleans shadows (regression guard for the no-behaviour-change requirement).

verification.evidence: === 42 passed, 0 failed === (was 33 before; +9 assertions across 3 new cases)

verification.command: test_boot_repair.sh with GUARD 3 neutered (system_is_uefi() { return 0; }) in a scratch copy
verification.evidence: === 38 passed, 4 failed === -- fails 'explains why it refused', 'names the override', 'does not claim shadows', 'real initramfs preserved'. Proves the new case actually catches the bug rather than passing vacuously.

verification.command: vm new bg && vm run bg 'sudo /usr/local/sbin/boot-repair'  (BIOS/GRUB sandbox)
verification.evidence: Guest confirmed BIOS-shaped first: no /sys/firmware/efi, no /boot fstab entry, findmnt /boot empty (GUARD 1 passes), no EFI//loader/ (GUARD 2 passes). boot-repair printed '[WARN] no /sys/firmware/efi -- this system booted via BIOS and has no ESP' and left /boot/vmlinuz-linux (17101312 b) and /boot/initramfs-linux.img (14957933 b) untouched. Exit 1 from the pre-existing 'no /boot entry in /etc/fstab' finding, which is BIOS noise, not a regression.

verification.command: vm run bg 'sudo systemctl poweroff' then vm run bg 'uname -r'
verification.evidence: Host-side VERDICT: clean poweroff (reached 'reboot: Power down'), then the guest booted again into 7.1.9-arch1-2 with both kernel files present. This is the exact scenario that previously left the guest permanently unbootable.
=== 42 passed, 0 failed === inside the BIOS guest as well as on the UEFI host.
No BIOS warning; '[ OK ] /boot mounted (/dev/nvme0n1p1)', ESP kernel and initramfs both OK. Confirms the required no-behaviour-change on kuhy's actual machine.
all hooks pass, including the 250-line cap and shellcheck

risks: A UEFI machine booted with efivars unavailable (e.g. an ISO rescue booted in legacy mode to repair a UEFI install) now refuses shadow cleanup. Mitigated by the --esp DEVICE override, which is named in the warning text itself.

The guard only covers the destructive path. A BIOS box still gets noisy FAIL lines from check_fstab_options and mount_esp, and run_preflight would abort kernel upgrades there. All are fail-closed and non-destructive; noted in the commit message rather than fixed, to keep this change narrow.
rollback: git revert the commit; boot-repair is self-contained and installed by copy, so re-run linux_configuration/scripts/boot_recovery/install.sh to push the reverted script to /usr/local/sbin.
After rollback, confirm ./boot-repair --dry-run on the UEFI host still reports '/boot mounted' and do NOT run it on any BIOS system -- the deletion bug is live again.
